identification.name: Borosilicate Glass (Pyrex® / BOROFLOAT® 33)
identification.common_form_notes: Laboratory glass, sight glasses, optical windows, mirror substrates
identification.notes: BOROFLOAT® 33 (Schott) and Pyrex® 7740 (Corning) are both borosilicate glasses with similar compositions and near-identical properties; BOROFLOAT® 33 data used here as it has more complete current datasheets. Tensile strength (0.025 GPa) is the flexural/bending strength (MOR) per DIN (German industrial standard) 52292; safe-load bending strength is 7 MPa. Maximum service temperature 450°C continuous, 500°C brief (<10 h). Hardness converted from Knoop 480 HK (Knoop hardness, per ISO 9385 — International Organization for Standardization) to HV (Vickers hardness) using HV ≈ HK/1.05. Thermal diffusivity is derived from thermal conductivity (k), density (ρ), and specific heat (Cp) — not an independently measured value.

typical_usage: Laboratory glassware, sight glasses, optical windows, mirror substrates for non-critical applications, MEMS (micro-electro-mechanical systems) wafers, semiconductor processing chambers, and telescope eyepiece blanks where moderate thermal expansion is acceptable.
